new_statements.quote: Stress in Tena Quichua generally falls on the penultimate syllable (as shown in the examples in (1) above). However, a subset of suffixes causes stress to fall on the last syllable of the word, including: the locative (LOC) suffix when added to polysyllabic words ending in a vowel (see example (5) above), third person singular /-n/ and plural /-nun/ present tense markers (see examples (6) above and (7)), and the suffix /-nɡax/ used to express future obligation (see example (8)). [...] There are also cases in which the addition of a suffix does not cause stress shift to the new penultimate syllable, as in the topic marker (TOP) /-ɡa/ (Orr 1991).

new_statements.relation_note: NOT in the READALL works list for this item; it was downloaded by the 2026-09-16 pass (see in our check folder) and lies inside the custody tree, so it was read here as the only openable Tena Quichua source. It agrees with the catalog's penultimate rule (penultimate stress) and refines it with the suffix-conditioned final-stress class, the extrametrical topic marker, variable accusative behaviour, and initial/second-syllable secondary stress. Describes exactly the tena1240 variety (Tena Quichua, quw, Napo above the Coca, Misahualli/Arajuno/Ansuc tributaries).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the word by default. A closed set of suffixes attracts stress to the final syllable: the locative /-i/ on polysyllabic vowel-final words (/ˈjaku-i/ > [jaˈkw-i] 'in the water'), the third-person present markers /-n/ (sg) and /-nun/ (pl) (/tiɡra-ˈnun/ 'they turn'), and the future-obligation suffix /-nɡax/ (/piti-nˈɡa-x/ 'in order to cut'). Some suffixes are extrametrical, i.e. adding them does not move stress to the new penult: the topic marker /-ɡa/ (citing Orr 1991) and, variably, the accusative /-ɾa/ (/ˈkwika-ɾa/ 'earthworm-ACC' vs /aiˈtʃa-ɾa/ 'meat-ACC').
new_statements.secondary_stress: p. 113: 'Last, there are some words where secondary stress may be perceived, either on the first or sometimes second syllable, as in (12) and (13).' Examples: /ˌjanapa-ɾj-aˈnun/ 'they are helping', /aˌʃanɡa-ˈɡuna/ 'baskets'; Figure 4 (p. 114) shows secondary stress on the initial syllable with penultimate primary stress in [ˌrimanuˈnau̯ka] 'they were talking to each other'. The authors call for an acoustic study; preliminary observation is that intensity and an f0 peak mark the stressed syllable and unstressed vowels are not reduced.
new_statements.exceptions: Final stress with the locative /-i/, 3sg /-n/, 3pl /-nun/ and /-nɡax/; no shift with the topic marker /-ɡa/ and variably with the accusative /-ɾa/ ('Whether or not penultimate stress is observed with /-ɾa/ may be due to several factors, including word order and placement within the discourse'). The authors state that 'more work on stress (and stress shift) in TQ is needed' (p. 114).
new_statements.identity_note: O'Rourke & Swanson 2013 describe Tena Quichua (ISO 639-3 quw), 'spoken in the Eastern Amazonian region of Ecuador on the Napo River above the mouth of the Rio Coca, primarily on three tributaries: the Misahualli, the Arajuno, and the Ansuc' (p. 107), i.e. the tena1240 variety itself, distinguished from Napo Quichua and Pastaza (Bobonaza) Quichua. Orr 1992 Runa shimi is a grammar of the same Tena variety per its title; its content could not be verified.

audit.reasoning: Quote check: the deciding sentence is verbatim on PDF p.1 of the held Orr 1991 excerpt (page image read), and the two exception passages are in the held scanned. The deciding source is a 1991 pedagogical lesson book (20-page excerpt), which is not the best available description, but the two better sources — O'Rourke & Swanson 2013 (JIPA Illustration, downloaded now, pp.113-114) and Grzech 2016 (SOAS PhD grammar sketch, already held, §2.1.2.2 p.44, pitch-track-checked) — both state that Tena Quichua stress falls on the penultimate syllable by default, so the penultimate (non-strict, word-domain) coding stands. They refine the exception set: besides Orr's antepenultimate interrogatives (íma-ra) and non-shifting topic =ga, stress is word-final with LOC -i on polysyllabic V-final hosts, 3P -nun, purposive -ngax (3S -n variably), and in disyllabic ideophones; secondary stress may fall on the first o
